title: Initialize Go module and cmd/internal package layout
body:
## Description
Set up the backend as a Go module (`github.com/rnikhori/paygate`) with the `cmd/api` entrypoint and empty `internal/{ledger,orders,payments,methods,settlements,webhooks,merchants,subscriptions,fraud,notifications}` packages per the repo structure in ARCHITECTURE.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `go.mod` created with module path and Go 1.23
- [ ] `cmd/api/main.go` builds and runs (even as a no-op server)
- [ ] `internal/` packages exist with a doc.go stating each package's single responsibility
- [ ] `internal/ledger` has no imports from any other `internal/*` package

title: Add docker-compose for local Postgres
body:
## Description
Provide a `docker-compose.yml` that brings up a local Postgres 16 instance with a persisted volume, matching the DB the API connects to in local dev.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docker compose up` starts Postgres on port 5432
- [ ] Credentials/db name are configurable via env vars with sane defaults
- [ ] Data persists across `docker compose down`/`up` via a named volume
- [ ] README documents the one-command local DB setup

title: Add golang-migrate tooling and initial migration runner
body:
## Description
Wire up `golang-migrate` (or equivalent) so schema changes are versioned SQL files under `backend/migrations`, runnable via a Makefile target against the local or CI database.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `make migrate-up` / `make migrate-down` work against local Postgres
- [ ] Migrations run automatically in CI before integration tests
- [ ] An empty baseline migration exists to prove the tool works end-to-end
- [ ] Migration naming convention documented (timestamp_description.up/down.sql)

title: Implement environment-based config loading
body:
## Description
Add a typed `Config` struct loaded from environment variables (with `.env` support for local dev) covering DB DSN, HTTP port, log level, and webhook signing secret.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Config fails fast with a clear error if a required var is missing
- [ ] `.env.example` committed listing every variable with a safe placeholder
- [ ] Config struct is passed explicitly into services (no global mutable state)
- [ ] Unit test covers missing-required-var failure path

title: Set up GitHub Actions CI for backend (lint, build, test)
body:
## Description
Add a workflow that runs on every PR touching `backend/`: `go vet`, `golangci-lint`, `go build ./...`, and `go test ./...` against a Postgres service container.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Workflow triggers on push/PR for `backend/**`
- [ ] Postgres service container is provisioned and migrations run before tests
- [ ] Workflow fails the PR check on any lint/test failure
- [ ] Build artifacts are cached between runs to keep CI fast

title: Set up GitHub Actions CI for frontend (lint, build, test)
body:
## Description
Add a workflow that runs on every PR touching `frontend/`: ESLint, TypeScript typecheck, unit tests, and a production build for each of dashboard/admin/checkout-widget.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Workflow triggers on push/PR for `frontend/**`
- [ ] Each of the three frontend apps is linted, typechecked, and built independently
- [ ] Node modules are cached between runs
- [ ] Workflow fails the PR check on any lint/typecheck/test/build failure

title: Add golangci-lint config and fix baseline issues
body:
## Description
Add a `.golangci.yml` enabling a sensible default linter set (govet, staticcheck, errcheck, unused) and fix any violations found on the initial scaffold so CI starts green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.golangci.yml` committed at repo root
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` passes with zero issues on current code
- [ ] Linter is invoked by the backend CI workflow
- [ ] Rationale for any disabled linters is documented inline in the config

title: Add pre-commit hooks for formatting
body:
## Description
Add a pre-commit hook (via `pre-commit` or a simple git hook script) that runs `gofmt`/`goimports` on staged Go files and `prettier` on staged frontend files.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hook installs via a documented one-line command
- [ ] Hook blocks the commit if formatting would change staged files, and reports which
- [ ] Hook runs in under 2 seconds for a typical small diff
- [ ] README documents how to install/skip the hook

title: Write CONTRIBUTING.md with local dev setup
body:
## Description
Document the full local setup path: clone, `docker compose up`, run migrations, start the API, start each frontend app, and run the test suites.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A new contributor can follow the doc start-to-finish with no undocumented steps
- [ ] Required tool versions (Go, Node, Docker) are listed
- [ ] Common troubleshooting (port conflicts, stale migrations) has a section
- [ ] Doc is linked from the root README

title: Add Makefile with common dev tasks
body:
## Description
Provide a root `Makefile` wrapping the repetitive commands (run API, migrate, test backend, test frontend, lint everything) so CI and contributors share one entrypoint.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `make run`, `make migrate-up`, `make test`, `make lint` all work from a clean checkout
- [ ] `make help` lists every target with a one-line description
- [ ] CI workflows call into the same Makefile targets (no drift between CI and local)
- [ ] Targets are no-op-safe to re-run (idempotent)

title: Design LedgerAccount schema and seed system accounts
body:
## Description
Create the `ledger_accounts` table and seed the fixed system accounts referenced throughout the design (`customer_suspense`, `gateway_fee_revenue`, `settlement_clearing`) plus a per-merchant `merchant_payable:<merchant_id>` account convention.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ledger_accounts` table has a unique, immutable `code` and a `type` (asset/liability/revenue)
- [ ] System accounts are created via a migration/seed, not ad hoc at runtime
- [ ] Merchant payable accounts are created automatically when a Merchant is activated
- [ ] Account codes are validated against a naming convention at creation time

title: Design JournalEntry schema with double-entry constraint
body:
## Description
Create the `journal_entries` table (immutable, append-only) grouped by a `transaction_ref`, where every row references a `ledger_account` and a signed amount, and rows sharing a `transaction_ref` must sum to zero.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Table is append-only: no UPDATE/DELETE grants at the DB role level
- [ ] Each row stores `transaction_ref`, `account_id`, `amount`, `currency`, `created_at`
- [ ] A `transaction_ref` always has at least 2 rows
- [ ] Schema documented in ARCHITECTURE.md's ledger section stays in sync with this migration

title: Implement PostJournalEntry enforcing balanced postings
body:
## Description
Add the single write path (`PostJournalEntry(ctx, transactionRef, entries []Entry)`) that every other service must use to move money — it rejects any call whose entries don't sum to zero per currency.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rejects (no partial write) if `sum(entries.amount) != 0` for any currency
- [ ] Writes all entries for a transaction in a single DB transaction
- [ ] Returns a domain error distinct from DB errors for the imbalance case
- [ ] No other package writes to `journal_entries` directly — enforced by code review checklist + a lint rule if feasible

title: Implement computed balance view per ledger account
body:
## Description
Expose `GetBalance(accountID)` as `SUM(journal_entries.amount) WHERE account_id = ?` — balances are never stored as a mutable counter, matching the design principle in ARCHITECTURE.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No `balance` column exists anywhere on `ledger_accounts`
- [ ] `GetBalance` is backed by an indexed query performant enough for dashboard use (<100ms at 100k entries/account in a benchmark)
- [ ] A materialized/cached balance (if added later) is explicitly out of scope here and flagged as a follow-up, not silently added
- [ ] Unit test proves balance matches hand-computed sum across a mixed set of postings

title: Add DB-level guard against unbalanced transactions
body:
## Description
Beyond the application-level check in `PostJournalEntry`, add a defense-in-depth DB constraint/trigger that rejects a `transaction_ref` whose entries don't net to zero, so a bug elsewhere can't corrupt the ledger.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A deferred constraint trigger fires at commit time per `transaction_ref`
- [ ] Directly inserting an unbalanced set of rows via raw SQL fails the transaction
- [ ] Trigger overhead is measured and acceptable (<10% write latency increase in benchmark)
- [ ] Migration includes a rollback that removes the trigger cleanly

title: Implement ledger posting for payment capture
body:
## Description
When a Payment transitions to `captured`, post a balanced journal entry moving funds from `customer_suspense` into the merchant's `merchant_payable:<id>` account net of the gateway fee, with the fee posted to `gateway_fee_revenue`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Capture posts exactly one `transaction_ref` with 3 balanced entries (suspense debit, merchant credit, fee revenue credit)
- [ ] Fee calculation is pulled from the merchant's configured fee schedule
- [ ] Posting happens in the same DB transaction as the Payment status update to `captured`
- [ ] Integration test covers a capture end-to-end and asserts resulting balances

title: Implement ledger posting for refunds
body:
## Description
On a full or partial Refund, post a reversing entry moving funds back out of `merchant_payable:<id>` (and proportionally reverse the fee if the fee policy requires it) into `customer_suspense`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Partial refund posts a proportional amount, not the full captured amount
- [ ] Refund posting references the original capture's `transaction_ref` for traceability
- [ ] A merchant cannot be refunded more than their available `merchant_payable` balance from that payment
- [ ] Test covers: full refund, two sequential partial refunds, over-refund rejection

title: Implement ledger posting for settlement clearing
body:
## Description
When a Settlement batch is finalized, post entries moving the batched amount from each merchant's `merchant_payable:<id>` into `settlement_clearing`, representing funds in transit to the merchant's bank.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One `transaction_ref` per merchant per settlement batch (not one giant unscoped entry)
- [ ] Only `captured` payments older than the settlement cutoff are included
- [ ] Posting is idempotent if the settlement job is retried after a partial failure
- [ ] Test covers a settlement batch spanning multiple payments for one merchant

title: Add idempotency guard on journal entry posting
body:
## Description
Ensure `PostJournalEntry` is safe to retry: a duplicate call with the same `transaction_ref` must not double-post, returning the original result instead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `transaction_ref` has a uniqueness constraint enforced at the DB level
- [ ] A retried post with an identical entry set returns success without creating new rows
- [ ] A retried post with a *different* entry set for the same `transaction_ref` is rejected with a clear error
- [ ] Concurrency test: two goroutines posting the same `transaction_ref` simultaneously result in exactly one set of rows

title: Build ledger account statement API
body:
## Description
Add an internal API returning a paginated list of journal entries for a given ledger account, ordered by time, for use by the dashboard's transaction history and by support/ops tooling.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Supports cursor-based pagination
- [ ] Supports filtering by date range
- [ ] Response includes running balance after each entry
- [ ] Endpoint is merchant-scoped (a merchant can only query their own `merchant_payable` account)

title: Add unit tests for the double-entry balance invariant
body:
## Description
Write a focused unit test suite that exercises every posting path (capture, refund, settlement) and asserts the fundamental invariant: sum of all journal entries across the whole ledger is always zero.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A property-based/table test posts random valid sequences and checks the global-zero invariant after each
- [ ] A test attempts an invalid posting and asserts it's rejected without side effects
- [ ] Tests run as part of backend CI
- [ ] Coverage report shows `internal/ledger` posting logic at >90%

title: Add migration for ledger_accounts and journal_entries tables
body:
## Description
Write the versioned SQL migration creating both core ledger tables with the indexes needed for the balance-computation and statement-API query patterns.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Index on `journal_entries(account_id, created_at)` for statement queries
- [ ] Index on `journal_entries(transaction_ref)` for idempotency lookups
- [ ] Foreign key from `journal_entries.account_id` to `ledger_accounts.id`
- [ ] Down migration cleanly drops both tables

title: Document the chart of accounts and naming convention
body:
## Description
Write a reference doc listing every ledger account type/pattern in the system (system accounts + per-merchant pattern), when each is debited/credited, and by which service.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every account referenced anywhere in the codebase appears in the doc
- [ ] Doc includes a worked example trace for a capture-then-refund scenario
- [ ] Doc lives at `docs/LEDGER.md` and is linked from ARCHITECTURE.md
- [ ] Reviewed by whoever implements the settlement epic, since it's the main consumer

title: Implement nightly ledger integrity check job
body:
## Description
Add a scheduled job that sums every journal entry across the entire ledger and asserts it equals zero, plus spot-checks that no account's entries alone are unbalanced beyond expected system accounts, alerting ops on failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Job runs on a schedule (configurable, default nightly) and on demand
- [ ] Job failure triggers the alerting path built in the Observability epic
- [ ] Job result (pass/fail + sums) is persisted for audit/history
- [ ] Job is read-only — it never attempts to "fix" the ledger itself

title: Add admin-only raw journal entry inspection API
body:
## Description
For debugging support tickets, add an admin API (used by the Admin/Ops Panel) that returns every journal entry for a given Payment's `transaction_ref`(s), unformatted.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Endpoint requires admin role, not accessible to merchants
- [ ] Returns entries grouped by `transaction_ref` in chronological order
- [ ] Access to this endpoint is itself audit-logged (who looked up what, when)
- [ ] Response includes account code, not just internal account ID, for readability

title: Design Merchant schema with status lifecycle
body:
## Description
Create the `merchants` table capturing legal/business name, business type, contact details, bank account reference, and a `status` field driving the onboarding state machine (`pending` → `under_review` → `activated` / `rejected`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `status` transitions are only possible via an explicit state-machine function, never a raw column update
- [ ] Table includes `created_at`/`updated_at` and a `status_history` relation or JSON log
- [ ] Unique constraint on business registration identifier (mock PAN/GST field)
- [ ] Migration committed with the above

title: Build merchant signup API
body:
## Description
Add `POST /v1/merchants/signup` creating a Merchant record in `pending` status plus an owner user account, kicking off the onboarding flow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Validates email uniqueness and basic field presence
- [ ] Creates the owner user with a securely hashed password
- [ ] Returns a session or a next-step token to continue onboarding
- [ ] Rejects duplicate signups with the standard `{error:{code,description,field}}` envelope

title: Build business details capture API
body:
## Description
Add an endpoint for a `pending` merchant to submit legal name, business type (individual/partnership/private limited/etc.), address, and mock PAN/GST identifiers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Business type drives which downstream KYC document types are required
- [ ] Partial submissions are saved as drafts (merchant can resume)
- [ ] Field-level validation errors use the field-tagged error envelope
- [ ] Submission transitions merchant to `under_review` once all required fields are present

title: Implement mock KYC document upload endpoint
body:
## Description
Add an endpoint accepting document uploads (e.g. mock PAN card, address proof) that stores file metadata and a reference, without performing any real verification against external registries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Accepts common image/PDF types with a size limit
- [ ] Stores documents with merchant-scoped access control
- [ ] Required document list is derived from the merchant's declared business type
- [ ] Clearly labeled in code/docs as a mock — no claim of real verification

title: Implement mock KYC verification workflow
body:
## Description
Add a rule-based mock verifier that evaluates an `under_review` merchant's submitted details/documents and either auto-approves, auto-rejects, or flags for manual review, simulating what a real KYC provider integration would return.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rules are configurable (e.g. missing required doc → reject; all present → approve)
- [ ] Result is recorded with a reason, visible to ops in the admin panel
- [ ] Flagged-for-review cases queue into the admin panel rather than auto-deciding
- [ ] Verification outcome drives the next status transition automatically

title: Build merchant activation flow
body:
## Description
Wire the terminal transition: once KYC passes (auto or manual), move the merchant to `activated`, which triggers API key generation (Auth epic) and ledger account creation (Ledger epic).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Activation is a single transactional operation across merchant status, API keys, and ledger account creation
- [ ] Activation triggers a welcome notification (stubbed until Notifications epic lands)
- [ ] A merchant cannot accept payments via the API before activation (enforced, not just UI-hidden)
- [ ] Activation event is emitted for any future listeners (webhooks, analytics)

title: Add bank account capture with mock penny-drop verification
body:
## Description
Add an endpoint for merchants to submit settlement bank account details, verified via a simulated "penny drop" (a mock micro-deposit + name-match check) before the account is eligible to receive settlements.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Account number + IFSC-style code format validated
- [ ] Mock verification returns a deterministic pass/fail based on test fixtures
- [ ] Unverified bank accounts block settlement eligibility
- [ ] Changing a verified bank account re-triggers verification

title: Implement merchant status transition audit log
body:
## Description
Record every status transition a merchant goes through (who/what triggered it, old status, new status, reason) for support and compliance visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every transition in the state machine writes an audit row, no exceptions
- [ ] Audit entries are immutable (insert-only)
- [ ] Admin panel can render a merchant's full history in order
- [ ] Audit log entries distinguish automated vs. manual (ops-triggered) transitions

title: Build merchant profile API for dashboard
body:
## Description
Add read/update endpoints so an activated merchant can view and edit non-sensitive business profile fields from the dashboard (display name, support email/phone, logo), separate from the immutable legal/KYC fields.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Legal/KYC fields are read-only after activation (require a separate re-verification flow to change)
- [ ] Editable fields are clearly distinguished in the API schema from locked ones
- [ ] Update endpoint is idempotent-safe for repeated identical submissions
- [ ] Changes are reflected immediately in the dashboard without re-login

title: Add email verification step during signup
body:
## Description
Require a merchant's owner email to be verified (click a tokenized link) before the merchant can proceed past basic signup into business-details submission.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Verification token expires after a configurable window
- [ ] Expired/used tokens show a clear re-send option
- [ ] Unverified merchants are blocked from submitting business details
- [ ] Resend is rate-limited to prevent spamming the mailbox

title: Write integration tests for the full onboarding happy path
body:
## Description
Write an end-to-end integration test exercising signup → business details → KYC docs → auto-approval → activation → API keys issued, against a real test database.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test runs against the migrated schema in CI, not mocks
- [ ] Asserts final state: merchant `activated`, ledger account exists, API key pair exists
- [ ] Covers at least one rejection-path variant (missing required doc)
- [ ] Test is part of the backend CI suite and fails the build on regression

title: Document the onboarding state machine
body:
## Description
Write a reference doc diagramming every merchant status, valid transitions, what triggers each, and which fields are required at each stage.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Includes a state diagram (mermaid or equivalent) matching the implemented code exactly
- [ ] Lists required fields per business type
- [ ] Doc lives at `docs/ONBOARDING.md`, linked from ARCHITECTURE.md
- [ ] Reviewed against the actual state machine code for drift before merging

title: Design ApiKey schema with test/live scoping
body:
## Description
Create the `api_keys` table storing `key_id` (public), a hash of `key_secret` (never stored plaintext), `mode` (test/live), `merchant_id`, and `status` (active/revoked).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `key_secret` is stored only as a salted hash
- [ ] `key_id` is globally unique and prefixed to indicate mode (e.g. `key_test_...` / `key_live_...`)
- [ ] A merchant can have multiple keys per mode (for rotation overlap)
- [ ] Migration committed with appropriate indexes

title: Generate API key pairs on merchant activation
body:
## Description
As part of the activation transaction (Onboarding epic), generate one test-mode and one live-mode key pair, returning the secret exactly once (never retrievable again).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Secret is shown to the merchant exactly once at generation time
- [ ] Secret generation uses a cryptographically secure random source
- [ ] Both key pairs are created atomically with the activation transaction
- [ ] Losing the secret requires rotation, not retrieval

title: Implement HTTP Basic auth middleware for server-to-server API
body:
## Description
Add middleware validating `key_id`/`key_secret` via HTTP Basic auth on every `/v1/*` server-to-server route, resolving the authenticated merchant and mode into request context.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Invalid/missing credentials return 401 with the standard error envelope
- [ ] Authenticated mode (test/live) is available to downstream handlers and enforced (test keys can't touch live data and vice versa)
- [ ] Secret comparison is constant-time to avoid timing attacks
- [ ] Middleware is covered by tests for valid, invalid, and malformed credentials

title: Implement API key rotation endpoint
body:
## Description
Add a dashboard endpoint to generate a new secret for an existing `key_id`, with a short overlap window where both old and new secrets work before the old is invalidated.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New secret shown once, same as initial generation
- [ ] Overlap window is configurable (default e.g. 24h) then old secret stops working automatically
- [ ] Rotation is logged to the audit trail
- [ ] Rotating a key doesn't change its `key_id`, so merchant-side config referencing the ID stays valid

title: Implement API key revocation endpoint
body:
## Description
Add a dashboard endpoint to immediately disable a key pair (e.g. on suspected compromise), with no overlap window.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Revoked key fails auth immediately, not after a delay
- [ ] Revocation requires owner/admin role, not viewer
- [ ] Revoking the last active live key for a merchant shows a confirmation warning (would block live payments)
- [ ] Revocation is logged to the audit trail with actor identity

title: Build dashboard session login/logout
body:
## Description
Implement email/password login issuing a server-side session (secure, httpOnly cookie) for dashboard users, plus logout invalidating the session.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Passwords hashed with a modern algorithm (bcrypt/argon2), never logged
- [ ] Session cookie is `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` at minimum
- [ ] Failed login attempts are rate-limited per account/IP
- [ ] Logout invalidates the session server-side, not just client-side cookie clear

title: Implement CSRF protection for dashboard session endpoints
body:
## Description
Add CSRF token issuance and validation for all state-changing dashboard requests authenticated via session cookie (server-to-server API-key auth is exempt, as it isn't cookie-based).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CSRF token is required on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE for session-authenticated routes
- [ ] Requests missing/mismatched tokens are rejected with 403
- [ ] Token is bound to the session, rotated on login
- [ ] Covered by a test attempting a cross-origin form-style request

title: Design RBAC roles for dashboard team members
body:
## Description
Define `owner`, `admin`, and `viewer` roles for a merchant's dashboard users, with a clear permission matrix (who can rotate keys, issue refunds, edit settings, view-only, etc.).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Permission matrix documented and reviewed before implementation
- [ ] Every merchant has exactly one `owner` at all times (can't demote/remove the last owner)
- [ ] Roles are stored per (merchant, user) pair, not globally on the user
- [ ] Matrix covers every sensitive action introduced by other epics (refunds, key rotation, payouts)

title: Implement role-based authorization middleware
body:
## Description
Add middleware enforcing the RBAC permission matrix on dashboard API routes, returning 403 for authenticated-but-unauthorized requests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each route declares its required role/permission explicitly (no implicit defaults)
- [ ] A `viewer` cannot perform any mutating action via direct API calls, even if the UI hides the button
- [ ] Authorization failures are distinguishable from authentication failures in logs (401 vs 403)
- [ ] Covered by tests for each role against a representative mutating and read-only route

title: Add team member invite flow
body:
## Description
Allow an `owner`/`admin` to invite another person by email with an assigned role; invitee sets a password via a tokenized invite link to join the merchant's dashboard team.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Invite tokens expire and are single-use
- [ ] Inviting an email that already has an account on another merchant is handled explicitly (reject or multi-merchant support, decide and document)
- [ ] Pending invites are listed and revocable before acceptance
- [ ] Accepting an invite immediately grants the assigned role, no extra approval step

title: Write tests for test-mode/live-mode data isolation
body:
## Description
Verify that a request authenticated with a test-mode key can never read or write data created under live mode for the same merchant, and vice versa.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test creates data in both modes and asserts cross-mode queries return empty/404, not the other mode's data
- [ ] Covers Orders, Payments, and Refunds list/detail endpoints at minimum
- [ ] Test fails loudly (not silently passes) if mode scoping is ever removed from a query
- [ ] Runs as part of backend CI

title: Document the authentication scheme for API integrators
body:
## Description
Write the developer-facing doc explaining HTTP Basic auth with key_id/key_secret, test vs. live mode, and how to rotate keys safely in production.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Includes a working curl example
- [ ] Explicitly warns against embedding live secrets in client-side code
- [ ] Describes the rotation overlap window behavior
- [ ] Linked from the main developer documentation entrypoint (Documentation epic)

title: Design reconciliation record schema
body:
## Description
Create a `reconciliation_records` table linking a settlement batch's expected ledger total to the actual settlement-engine-reported total, with a status (`matched`/`break`) per batch per merchant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One record per (settlement_batch, merchant) pair
- [ ] Stores both the ledger-derived amount and the settlement-reported amount for comparison
- [ ] Status defaults to unresolved until the reconciliation job runs
- [ ] Migration committed with appropriate foreign keys

title: Implement daily reconciliation job
body:
## Description
Add a scheduled job comparing, for each settled batch, the ledger's `settlement_clearing` totals against the Settlement engine's recorded payout amounts, writing a `reconciliation_records` row per comparison.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Job is idempotent — re-running for an already-reconciled batch doesn't duplicate records
- [ ] Job covers all batches settled since the last successful run, not just "yesterday"
- [ ] Job completion/failure is logged and feeds the Observability alerting
- [ ] Runs against a read-replica-safe query pattern if one exists (otherwise noted as a future optimization)

title: Implement break/mismatch detection
body:
## Description
Within the reconciliation job, flag any batch where the ledger-derived and settlement-reported amounts differ by more than a configurable tolerance as a `break`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tolerance is configurable (default zero — any mismatch is a break)
- [ ] A break captures the delta amount and which side (ledger vs settlement) is higher
- [ ] Breaks are surfaced immediately to the alerting path, not just batch-reported
- [ ] Test fixture simulates a deliberately broken settlement amount and confirms detection

title: Build reconciliation break report API
body:
## Description
Add an internal API returning open and historical reconciliation breaks with filtering by date range and merchant, for the admin panel to consume.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Supports filtering by status (open/resolved) and date range
- [ ] Includes enough detail per break to start investigating without a separate query (batch id, merchant, delta, both amounts)
- [ ] Paginated for large result sets
- [ ] Admin-only access, audit-logged

title: Build admin UI for reconciliation breaks
body:
## Description
Add a view in the Admin/Ops Panel listing open reconciliation breaks with drill-down into the underlying ledger entries and settlement batch detail.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] List view sortable by delta amount and date
- [ ] Drill-down links directly to the admin ledger inspection view for the affected payments
- [ ] Open breaks are visually distinct from resolved ones
- [ ] Empty state clearly communicates "no open breaks" rather than looking broken

title: Implement manual break resolution action
body:
## Description
Allow an ops user to mark a reconciliation break as resolved with a required free-text note explaining the resolution, for audit purposes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Resolution requires a non-empty note
- [ ] Resolved breaks record which admin user resolved them and when
- [ ] Resolving a break doesn't retroactively alter any ledger/settlement data — it's a record-keeping action only
- [ ] Resolved breaks remain visible in a historical/filtered view

title: Add reconciliation summary CSV export
body:
## Description
Allow ops to export a date-ranged reconciliation summary (batches checked, breaks found, breaks resolved) as CSV from the admin panel.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Export respects the same filters as the on-screen report
- [ ] CSV includes a header row with clear column names
- [ ] Large exports stream rather than buffering the whole file in memory
- [ ] Export action is audit-logged (who exported what range)

title: Write tests simulating a ledger/settlement mismatch
body:
## Description
Write an integration test that deliberately creates a settlement record disagreeing with the ledger total and asserts the reconciliation job flags it as a break with the correct delta.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test covers both directions (ledger higher, settlement higher)
- [ ] Test asserts the break record's delta matches the injected discrepancy exactly
- [ ] Test asserts a matching (non-break) case does NOT create a break record
- [ ] Runs as part of backend CI

title: Implement per-API-key token-bucket rate limiter
body:
## Description
Add middleware enforcing a token-bucket rate limit keyed by `key_id`, independent per merchant and mode, so one merchant's traffic can't exhaust another's quota.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bucket refill rate and burst size are configurable per merchant tier
- [ ] Limiter state is shared correctly across multiple API instances (not per-process only)
- [ ] Requests over the limit are rejected before hitting business logic
- [ ] Unit test covers burst-then-refill behavior deterministically

title: Add configurable rate limits per merchant tier
body:
## Description
Allow different default rate limits based on a merchant's tier/plan (e.g. standard vs. high-volume), overridable per merchant for special cases.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tier-to-limit mapping is configuration, not hardcoded per merchant
- [ ] Per-merchant override takes precedence over tier default when set
- [ ] Changing a merchant's tier/override takes effect without a service restart
- [ ] Admin panel can view (and later, set) a merchant's effective limit

title: Return standard 429 response with Retry-After
body:
## Description
When a request is rejected for exceeding the rate limit, return HTTP 429 with the standard error envelope plus a `Retry-After` header indicating when the client can retry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `Retry-After` value is accurate to the bucket's actual refill timing, not a fixed constant
- [ ] Error body uses the same `{error:{code,description}}` shape as all other errors
- [ ] Rate-limit rejections are logged distinctly from auth failures
- [ ] Documented in the API reference so integrators know to respect the header

title: Implement request size limits and payload validation middleware
body:
## Description
Add middleware rejecting oversized request bodies before they reach handlers, and centralizing JSON schema/field validation so every endpoint reports errors in a consistent shape.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Oversized bodies are rejected with 413 before full body parsing completes
- [ ] Validation errors include the offending field name in the error envelope
- [ ] Limits are configurable per route where payload size legitimately differs (e.g. document upload vs. JSON API)
- [ ] Covered by tests for at-limit, over-limit, and malformed-JSON cases

title: Add centralized request logging middleware
body:
## Description
Add middleware logging every request's method, path, authenticated `key_id` (or session user), latency, and response status in structured form, as the single source for API traffic analysis.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Logs never include request/response bodies containing secrets (card numbers, key secrets, passwords)
- [ ] Every request gets a correlation/request ID surfaced in both the log and the response headers
- [ ] Logging middleware runs for every route with negligible overhead (<1ms p50)
- [ ] Format matches the structured logging convention set in the Observability epic

title: Implement shared Idempotency-Key middleware
body:
## Description
Centralize the `Idempotency-Key` header handling described in ARCHITECTURE.md into one middleware usable by every mutating endpoint (Orders, Payments, Refunds, Payouts), rather than each handler reimplementing it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Same key + same request body replays the original response without re-executing side effects
- [ ] Same key + different body returns a 409-style conflict error
- [ ] Stored idempotency records expire after a reasonable retention window
- [ ] At least three different endpoints (from different epics) are migrated to use this shared middleware, not a per-endpoint copy

title: Add abuse detection with temporary key lockout
body:
## Description
Detect repeated authentication failures against a given `key_id` or IP in a short window and temporarily lock out further attempts, to blunt credential-guessing attacks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Lockout threshold and duration are configurable
- [ ] Lockout applies per key_id and per IP independently
- [ ] Legitimate key owner can see lockout status/reason in the dashboard
- [ ] Lockout events are logged for security review

title: Write load test for rate limiter under burst traffic
body:
## Description
Write a load test that fires a burst of concurrent requests from a single API key well above its configured limit and asserts the limiter holds the line without crashing or leaking memory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test confirms excess requests are rejected (not queued indefinitely or silently dropped)
- [ ] Test confirms other merchants' requests are unaffected during the burst
- [ ] Test measures and reports limiter overhead under load
- [ ] Results/thresholds documented so future regressions are detectable

title: Set up structured JSON logging across backend services
body:
## Description
Replace any ad hoc `fmt.Println`/plain-text logging with a structured JSON logger used consistently across all backend packages, including log level and contextual fields.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One logging library/wrapper used project-wide, no direct stdlib `log` calls in business code
- [ ] Log level configurable via the Config struct from the Setup epic
- [ ] Every log line includes at minimum: timestamp, level, service/package, message
- [ ] Secrets (API key secrets, passwords, full card numbers) are never logged, enforced by a redaction helper

title: Add request ID / trace ID propagation
body:
## Description
Generate a request ID at the API gateway middleware layer and propagate it through all logs and downstream calls for a given request, so a single request's full log trail can be reconstructed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Request ID is generated if not supplied, or honored if a client supplies `X-Request-ID`
- [ ] ID appears in every log line emitted while handling that request, including background work it enqueues
- [ ] ID is returned in the response headers
- [ ] Verified with a test that traces one request's ID through at least two internal layers

title: Instrument API latency and error-rate metrics
body:
## Description
Expose Prometheus-compatible metrics for request latency (histogram, by route) and error rate (counter, by route and status class) from the API service.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `/metrics` endpoint exposed and scrapeable
- [ ] Latency histogram buckets are tuned for typical API response times (ms-scale)
- [ ] High-cardinality labels (like raw path params) are normalized to avoid metric explosion
- [ ] Metrics endpoint itself is excluded from rate limiting/auth as appropriate for internal scraping

title: Instrument ledger posting metrics
body:
## Description
Add metrics specific to the ledger: postings per second, posting latency, and a counter for balance-invariant check failures, since the ledger is the system's most correctness-critical component.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Invariant-failure counter is wired to page/alert immediately (not just a dashboard number)
- [ ] Posting latency is broken down by posting type (capture/refund/settlement)
- [ ] Metrics don't leak merchant-identifying labels into a globally-scraped metrics endpoint
- [ ] Verified against the nightly integrity check job from the Ledger epic

title: Add distributed tracing for the payment authorize/capture flow
body:
## Description
Instrument spans across the full authorize → capture path (API handler → payment method adapter → ledger posting → webhook emit) so a slow or failing payment can be diagnosed end-to-end.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single trace ID connects all spans for one payment attempt
- [ ] Spans include enough attributes (payment ID, method, outcome) to filter in a tracing UI
- [ ] Tracing overhead is negligible when sampling is enabled
- [ ] Verified by inspecting a captured trace for a real local test payment

title: Build a basic Grafana dashboard config for API health
body:
## Description
Provide a checked-in Grafana dashboard JSON (provisioned via config, not manually clicked together) showing request rate, latency percentiles, and error rate for the API service.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dashboard JSON lives in the repo (e.g. `infra/grafana/`) and loads via provisioning
- [ ] Panels cover p50/p95/p99 latency and 4xx/5xx rate at minimum
- [ ] Dashboard is scoped to be useful without requiring manual query editing
- [ ] README explains how to point it at a running Prometheus instance locally

title: Implement alerting rule for ledger imbalance
body:
## Description
Wire an alert (e.g. via Alertmanager or equivalent) that fires immediately when the ledger balance-invariant-failure metric or the nightly integrity job reports a nonzero global sum.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Alert fires within minutes of the underlying metric/job reporting a problem
- [ ] Alert routing/notification target is configurable (documented, even if just a webhook/log in this clone)
- [ ] Alert includes enough context to start investigating without re-querying from scratch
- [ ] Test simulates the failure condition and confirms the alert rule evaluates to firing

title: Implement alerting rule for webhook delivery failure spike
body:
## Description
Add an alert that fires when the rate of failed webhook deliveries (from the Webhooks epic's delivery log) exceeds a threshold over a rolling window, indicating a systemic issue rather than one flaky merchant endpoint.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Alert distinguishes "one merchant's endpoint is down" (expected, not alertable) from "many merchants failing" (systemic, alertable)
- [ ] Threshold and window are configurable
- [ ] Alert links to the webhook delivery log for investigation
- [ ] Covered by a test or simulated scenario proving the threshold logic works

title: Add health check and readiness endpoints
body:
## Description
Add `/healthz` (liveness) and `/readyz` (readiness, checking DB connectivity) endpoints on the API service for use by local tooling and any future orchestration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `/healthz` always returns 200 if the process is up, no dependency checks
- [ ] `/readyz` returns 503 if the DB connection pool can't reach Postgres
- [ ] Both endpoints are excluded from auth, rate limiting, and request-body logging noise
- [ ] Covered by a test for both the healthy and DB-down cases

title: Document logging and metrics conventions
body:
## Description
Write a short reference for contributors adding a new service/package: what fields every log line must have, naming conventions for new metrics, and how to avoid high-cardinality label mistakes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Doc gives a concrete "do this, not that" example for logs and for metrics
- [ ] Doc explains the redaction helper and what must never be logged
- [ ] Doc lives at `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md`, linked from ARCHITECTURE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md
- [ ] Reviewed against what was actually implemented in this epic, not aspirational

title: Define Order data model and DB migration
body:
## Description
Create the `orders` table and Go struct per the domain model in ARCHITECTURE.md: merchant_id, amount, currency, receipt, status, notes (jsonb), timestamps.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Migration creates `orders` table with indexes on merchant_id and receipt
- [ ] Receipt is unique per merchant
- [ ] Go struct + repository methods (Create, GetByID) implemented
- [ ] Migration is reversible (down migration)

title: POST /v1/orders — create order endpoint
body:
## Description
Implement order creation per the API design principles (API-key auth, consistent error envelope).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Validates amount > 0 and currency == INR
- [ ] Returns 201 with full order object on success
- [ ] Returns `{error:{code,description,field}}` on validation failure
- [ ] Order starts in `created` status

title: Idempotency-Key handling on order creation
body:
## Description
Enforce the Idempotency-Key header behavior described in ARCHITECTURE.md §4 for the create-order endpoint specifically.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Same key + same body replays the original response (no duplicate order created)
- [ ] Same key + different body returns 400 with a clear error code
- [ ] Idempotency keys expire after 24h
- [ ] Idempotency store is a separate table keyed by (merchant_id, key)

title: GET /v1/orders/:id — retrieve a single order
body:
## Description
Fetch one order by ID, scoped to the authenticated merchant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 404 if the order belongs to a different merchant (not 403 — avoid leaking existence)
- [ ] Response includes embedded payment summary (count, amount_paid)
- [ ] Response shape matches documented schema

title: GET /v1/orders — list orders with pagination and filters
body:
## Description
List endpoint supporting cursor-based pagination and filtering by status, date range, and receipt.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cursor pagination with `count` and `skip`/`from`/`to` matching Razorpay-style query params
- [ ] Default page size capped (e.g. 100)
- [ ] Filters combine with AND semantics
- [ ] Results ordered newest-first by default

title: Track amount_due / amount_paid on Order for partial payments
body:
## Description
An order can be paid across multiple Payment attempts (e.g. partial payment links). Track running totals on the order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `amount_paid` updates transactionally when a Payment captures
- [ ] Order `status` flips to `paid` only when amount_paid >= amount
- [ ] `amount_due` is a computed field (amount - amount_paid), not stored redundantly

title: Support arbitrary key/value notes on Order
body:
## Description
Merchants attach free-form metadata (e.g. internal order ref, customer ID) to an order via a `notes` field.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `notes` stored as jsonb, max 15 keys, each value max 256 chars (matches Razorpay's documented limits)
- [ ] Notes are returned verbatim on retrieval
- [ ] Notes are searchable is explicitly out of scope — documented as such

title: Reject duplicate receipts per merchant with a clear error
body:
## Description
Receipt uniqueness is enforced at the DB level (see migration issue); surface a friendly, documented error when violated instead of a raw constraint error.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Returns 400 with code `RECEIPT_ALREADY_EXISTS` and the field name
- [ ] Error message includes the conflicting order's id for merchant convenience
- [ ] Covered by an integration test

title: Integration tests for the full order lifecycle
body:
## Description
End-to-end test covering create → list → retrieve → paid transition, against a real Postgres test database.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Spins up a test DB (testcontainers or similar)
- [ ] Covers happy path and the idempotency-conflict path
- [ ] Runs in CI on every PR touching `internal/orders`

title: Write API reference docs for the Orders endpoints
body:
## Description
Document all Orders endpoints in the developer portal (see Documentation epic for the portal itself) with request/response examples.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every endpoint has a curl example and a sample JSON response
- [ ] Error codes table included
- [ ] Cross-linked from the Payments docs

title: Define Payment data model and state machine enum
body:
## Description
Create the `payments` table and the state machine described in ARCHITECTURE.md §3 (`created → authorized → captured → settled`, plus `failed`/`refunded`/`disputed`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Status stored as a constrained enum/check-constraint, not a free string
- [ ] Foreign key to `orders`, nullable method-detail reference
- [ ] Migration includes indexes on order_id and merchant_id+status

title: Enforce legal state transitions only
body:
## Description
A central transition-guard function rejects any transition not explicitly allowed by the state machine (e.g. `captured → authorized` must be impossible).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Transition table defined as data, not scattered if/else
- [ ] Illegal transition attempts return a typed error and are logged
- [ ] Unit tests enumerate every legal and illegal transition pair

title: POST /v1/payments — initiate a payment against an order
body:
## Description
Create a Payment row in `created` status and dispatch to the selected method adapter's `Authorize`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rejects if order is already fully paid
- [ ] Rejects if `method` is not one of card/upi/netbanking/wallet
- [ ] Returns the adapter's next-action (e.g. redirect URL) when applicable

title: Generic adapter dispatch via PaymentMethodAdapter interface
body:
## Description
Implement the dispatch layer that routes a Payment to its method's adapter implementation, per the interface in ARCHITECTURE.md §5.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `PaymentMethodAdapter` interface defined with Authorize/Capture/Refund/HandleCallback
- [ ] Adapter registry keyed by method name, no reflection/magic strings in call sites
- [ ] Adding a new method requires no changes outside `internal/methods/`

title: Capture step with manual vs. auto-capture configuration
body:
## Description
Support Razorpay-style `payment_capture` flag on the order: auto-capture immediately after authorization, or require an explicit Capture API call.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Merchant sets capture mode at order-creation time
- [ ] Manual-capture payments auto-expire (see separate expiry issue) if not captured in time
- [ ] Capture amount can be ≤ authorized amount (partial capture)

title: GET /v1/payments/:id — retrieve a payment
body:
## Description
Fetch a single payment with its method details and current status.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Scoped to the authenticated merchant (404 for others' payments)
- [ ] Includes a `method_details` sub-object shaped per method
- [ ] Includes `error_code`/`error_description` when status is `failed`

title: GET /v1/payments — list with filters
body:
## Description
List payments filterable by status, method, order_id, and date range.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pagination consistent with the Orders list endpoint
- [ ] Filter combinations covered by tests
- [ ] Response time acceptable with 100k+ row table (index-backed filters)

title: Enforce Idempotency-Key on payment creation
body:
## Description
Same idempotency contract as Orders, applied to `POST /v1/payments`, including the create-payment-against-order path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Replays with identical body return the original payment unmodified
- [ ] Replays with a different body return 400
- [ ] Shared idempotency middleware reused from Orders (no duplicated logic)

title: Define payment failure reason codes and mapping
body:
## Description
Establish a canonical set of failure reasons (e.g. `insufficient_funds`, `card_declined`, `otp_timeout`) that every adapter maps its mock failures onto.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reason codes documented in one shared enum used by all adapters
- [ ] Each adapter's mock failure modes map to a reason code (no adapter invents its own)
- [ ] Surfaced in the API response and in webhook payloads

title: Allow retrying a failed payment with a new attempt
body:
## Description
A failed Payment doesn't block further attempts on the same Order — the merchant/customer can retry with a new Payment row.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New Payment row created, linked to the same order
- [ ] Order status unaffected by prior failed attempts
- [ ] Dashboard shows all attempts against an order, most recent first

title: Support multiple partial payments against one order
body:
## Description
Allow more than one captured Payment to apply toward a single Order's amount (needed for Payment Links' partial-payment feature).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sum of captured payments cannot exceed order amount
- [ ] Order flips to `paid` only once fully covered
- [ ] Covered by a dedicated integration test

title: Auto-expire manual-capture payments left uncaptured
body:
## Description
A background job transitions `authorized` payments to `failed` if not captured within the configured window (Razorpay uses ~5 minutes to a few hours depending on method).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Configurable expiry window per method
- [ ] Job runs on a schedule and is idempotent/safe to run concurrently
- [ ] Emits the same domain event as any other failure

title: Emit domain events on every payment state transition
body:
## Description
Every transition (authorized, captured, failed, refunded, etc.) publishes a domain event consumed by the webhook dispatcher and settlement engine, per the event-driven design in ARCHITECTURE.md §2.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Event includes payment id, old status, new status, timestamp
- [ ] Event published in the same DB transaction as the state change (outbox pattern) to avoid lost events
- [ ] At-least-once delivery to consumers

title: Prevent double-capture under concurrent requests
body:
## Description
Two concurrent capture requests for the same payment must not both succeed — use row-level locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) around the capture transition.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Concurrent capture attempts: exactly one succeeds, the other gets a clear "already captured" error
- [ ] Verified with a concurrency test (parallel goroutines hitting the same payment)
- [ ] No ledger entries are double-posted

title: Reject capture amount exceeding authorized amount
body:
## Description
Validation guard so a capture request can't claim more than was authorized.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Returns 400 with code `CAPTURE_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_AUTHORIZED`
- [ ] Boundary-tested at exactly-equal and one-paisa-over
- [ ] Covered by a unit test

title: Unit tests for the full payment state machine
body:
## Description
Exhaustive table-driven tests over every (current_state, event) pair, verifying the resulting state or rejection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 100% of transition table entries covered
- [ ] Runs in under 1s (no real DB/network in these tests)
- [ ] Added to CI as a required check

title: Write API reference docs for the Payments endpoints
body:
## Description
Document create/retrieve/list/capture endpoints, the state machine diagram, and failure reason codes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] State diagram embedded (reuse ARCHITECTURE.md diagram)
- [ ] Full failure-reason-code table included
- [ ] Example request/response for each method

title: Card tokenization endpoint — never persist raw PAN
body:
## Description
Accept raw card details only transiently in-memory, issue an opaque token, and persist only token + last4 + network + expiry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Raw PAN/CVV never written to logs or the database
- [ ] Token is a non-guessable opaque identifier
- [ ] Covered by a test asserting no PAN substring appears in stored rows

title: Mock BIN detection and network identification
body:
## Description
Derive card network (Visa/Mastercard/RuPay/Amex) and issuing bank from the card number's first 6-8 digits, using a small embedded BIN table (mocked, not a real BIN database).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Returns network for common test BIN ranges
- [ ] Unknown BIN falls back to `unknown` network, doesn't error
- [ ] Unit tested against a fixed BIN fixture table

title: Define CardPaymentMethodDetail schema
body:
## Description
Polymorphic method-detail table/struct for cards: last4, network, expiry_month, expiry_year, token_id, cardholder name.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One-to-one with a Payment row
- [ ] No raw card number or CVV columns exist anywhere in the schema
- [ ] Expiry stored in a way that supports the expired-card validation issue

title: Implement Authorize for the card adapter
body:
## Description
Wire the card adapter's `Authorize` method: tokenize, validate, then hand off to the mock 3DS step.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Returns a `next_action` pointing to the mock 3DS redirect URL
- [ ] Payment moves to an intermediate `authorizing`-equivalent state until 3DS completes
- [ ] Expired or malformed card rejected before any 3DS step starts

title: Mock 3DS / OTP redirect page
body:
## Description
A simple hosted page simulating the bank's 3DS/OTP challenge — enter any 6-digit code, with a "force fail" test code for negative-path testing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Correct-looking OTP (any 6 digits except the reserved fail code) succeeds
- [ ] Reserved fail code (e.g. `000000`) simulates OTP failure
- [ ] Page is theme-able per merchant (basic logo/color) to mirror real redirect pages

title: 3DS callback handler updates payment status
body:
## Description
After the mock 3DS page posts back, update the Payment to `authorized` or `failed` and redirect the browser to the merchant's callback URL.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Callback is signed/validated so it can't be spoofed by the browser
- [ ] Redirect includes payment_id and status as query params, matching documented contract
- [ ] Idempotent — a replayed callback doesn't double-process

title: Mock card network response simulator
body:
## Description
Simulate network-level responses (approve/decline/insufficient_funds/timeout) driven by special test card numbers, matching the pattern real gateways' sandbox modes use.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Documented table of test card numbers → forced outcome
- [ ] Timeout outcome actually delays the response to exercise client timeout handling
- [ ] Unmapped card numbers default to "approve" in test mode

title: Allow retrying a declined card payment
body:
## Description
On decline, let the customer retry with a different card without re-creating the order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New Payment attempt created, previous one stays `failed`
- [ ] Checkout widget surfaces the decline reason before offering retry
- [ ] Retry count is capped (configurable) to deter brute-forcing card numbers

title: Save card token for future use (opt-in)
body:
## Description
Let a customer opt in at checkout to save their tokenized card against their identifier for faster future checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Requires explicit customer consent checkbox, not default-on
- [ ] Saved token is reusable only by the same merchant + customer pairing
- [ ] CVV is never stored even for saved cards

title: List and delete saved cards in the merchant dashboard
body:
## Description
Surface a customer's saved cards (for support/debugging in the dashboard's customer view) with the ability to delete a token.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Only last4/network/expiry shown, never a full number
- [ ] Deleting a token immediately makes it unusable for future charges
- [ ] Action is audit-logged (see Security & Compliance epic)

title: Require CVV re-entry when charging a saved card
body:
## Description
Even for a saved/tokenized card, require fresh CVV entry at charge time (CVV is never stored), matching real-world card-on-file behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Charge request rejected without a CVV field when using a saved token
- [ ] CVV is validated transiently and never persisted
- [ ] Covered by a test asserting CVV absence is rejected

title: Card capture endpoint (post-authorization capture)
body:
## Description
Wire the card adapter's `Capture` for manual-capture flows, reusing the generic capture-amount validation from the Payments core epic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Capture against an expired authorization window is rejected
- [ ] Partial capture supported (amount ≤ authorized)
- [ ] Capture result updates ledger via the standard event path

title: Card refund via adapter Refund()
body:
## Description
Implement the card adapter's `Refund`, simulating a 3-5 "business day" refund-to-source delay via a scheduled status update.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Refund created immediately in `pending` state, flips to `processed` after the simulated delay
- [ ] Refund amount validated against remaining refundable amount
- [ ] Reuses the shared Refund entity from the Refunds epic (no card-specific refund table)

title: Reject expired card at authorize time
body:
## Description
Validate expiry_month/expiry_year against the current date before attempting authorization, instead of letting it fail downstream.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Expired card returns a clear `CARD_EXPIRED` error before any 3DS step starts
- [ ] Boundary-tested on the expiry month's last day
- [ ] Unit tested with a fixed "current date" injected for determinism

title: Rate-limit OTP retry attempts per payment
body:
## Description
Cap the number of OTP attempts on the mock 3DS page to prevent brute-force guessing, mirroring real bank behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Max 3 attempts per payment, then the payment is force-failed
- [ ] Attempt counter resets only on a new Payment, not on page reload
- [ ] Covered by an integration test

title: Unit tests for the card adapter's mock response matrix
body:
## Description
Table-driven tests covering every test-card-number → outcome mapping defined in the network response simulator.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every documented test card number has a corresponding test case
- [ ] Timeout case asserts on elapsed time, not just outcome
- [ ] Added as a required CI check for `internal/methods/card`

title: Write a card integration guide for merchants
body:
## Description
Developer-portal page explaining card tokenization, 3DS redirect handling, and the test card number table.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Includes a copy-pasteable client-side tokenization example
- [ ] Test card table matches the implementation exactly (kept in sync, not duplicated by hand)
- [ ] Links to the Payments state-machine docs

title: UPI VPA format validation
body:
## Description
Validate a Virtual Payment Address (e.g. `name@bank`) against UPI's documented format rules before attempting a Collect request.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rejects malformed VPAs with a clear error before hitting the mock switch
- [ ] Accepts the standard `handle@psp` shape
- [ ] Unit tested against valid/invalid fixture lists

title: UPI Collect flow — request-to-pay API
body:
## Description
Implement the Collect flow: PayGate sends a payment request to the customer's VPA via the mock switch, customer approves/declines on their (simulated) UPI app.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Payment enters a `pending` state immediately, resolved asynchronously
- [ ] Request includes amount, payee VPA, and a reference note
- [ ] Matches the Payment state machine's `created → authorized/failed` path

title: UPI Intent flow — deep link generation
body:
## Description
Generate a `upi://pay?...` style intent URI the checkout widget can hand to installed UPI apps, for mobile web checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] URI includes payee VPA, amount, transaction ref, matching the real UPI intent URI spec
- [ ] Falls back to Collect flow when not on a mobile browser
- [ ] Unit tested for correct URI encoding of special characters in notes

title: Mock UPI switch simulating approve/decline/timeout
body:
## Description
A standalone mock component that plays the role of NPCI's UPI switch: receives the Collect/Intent request and asynchronously calls back approve, decline, or times out, selectable via a test VPA suffix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test VPAs like `success@mock`, `fail@mock`, `timeout@mock` drive deterministic outcomes
- [ ] Timeout outcome waits past the configured UPI timeout window before resolving
- [ ] Runs as an isolated internal package so it can be swapped for a real switch later

title: UPI payment status polling endpoint
body:
## Description
While the customer approves on their UPI app, the checkout widget polls payment status.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Lightweight endpoint returning just `{status}`, not the full payment object
- [ ] Rate-limited per payment to prevent poll storms
- [ ] Widget backs off polling interval exponentially

title: UPI Collect request expiry
body:
## Description
A Collect request not approved within a configurable window (Razorpay uses a few minutes) auto-expires to `failed`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Background job or scheduled check expires stale pending UPI payments
- [ ] Expiry reason code is distinct from a declined payment
- [ ] Covered by a test using a fast-forwarded clock

title: Async callback handler from the mock UPI switch
body:
## Description
The mock switch calls back into PayGate asynchronously (not inline with the original request) to resolve a pending UPI payment, exercising the same async-callback pattern a real integration would use.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Callback authenticated via a shared secret/signature
- [ ] Idempotent against duplicate callbacks for the same payment
- [ ] Triggers the standard domain-event path on resolution

title: UPI refund support via adapter
body:
## Description
Implement the UPI adapter's `Refund`, simulating near-instant UPI refund settlement (faster than card refunds).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Refund resolves to `processed` faster than the card refund simulation
- [ ] Reuses the shared Refund entity
- [ ] Partial refunds supported

title: Mock VPA handle directory by bank suffix
body:
## Description
A small lookup table mapping VPA suffixes (`@mockbank1`, `@mockbank2`, ...) to display bank names, used in UI and validation messaging.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] At least 5 mock banks represented
- [ ] Unknown suffix still passes basic format validation but shows as "Unknown bank" in UI
- [ ] Centralized so adding a mock bank requires one file change

title: UPI Intent QR code generation for desktop checkout
body:
## Description
On desktop, render the Intent URI as a scannable QR code so a customer can pay from their phone's UPI app.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] QR encodes the same URI as the mobile Intent deep link
- [ ] QR regenerates if the underlying payment is retried
- [ ] Rendered client-side in the checkout widget, no server round-trip per render

title: Mark UPI payment failed after timeout threshold
body:
## Description
If the mock switch doesn't resolve within the documented timeout window, force the payment to `failed` with a `upi_timeout` reason rather than leaving it pending indefinitely.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Timeout threshold configurable, defaults matching real UPI (~2-3 minutes for Collect)
- [ ] Works even if the mock switch never calls back at all
- [ ] Covered by a test simulating a switch that never responds

title: Allow resending an expired UPI Collect request
body:
## Description
Let the customer/merchant trigger a fresh Collect request for the same order after the first one expired, without re-entering order details.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Creates a new Payment attempt, previous stays `failed`
- [ ] Previous expired request can no longer be approved (switch rejects late callbacks)
- [ ] UI clearly distinguishes "expired, resend" from "declined"

title: Integration tests for UPI Collect and Intent flows
body:
## Description
End-to-end tests exercising both flows against the mock switch, including the approve/decline/timeout paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Covers Collect approve, Collect decline, Collect timeout, Intent approve
- [ ] Asserts correct domain events are published for each
- [ ] Runs in CI against a real test DB

title: Load test the mock UPI switch under concurrent callbacks
body:
## Description
Verify the async callback handler and idempotency guard hold up under many simultaneous UPI resolutions, since UPI's share of transaction volume is the highest of all methods in real Indian gateways.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Load test script simulates N concurrent payments resolving within a short window
- [ ] No lock contention errors or lost updates observed
- [ ] Results documented with a baseline throughput number

title: Write a UPI integration guide for merchants
body:
## Description
Developer-portal page covering Collect vs Intent, the test VPA suffixes that drive mock outcomes, and QR code embedding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Explains when to use Collect vs Intent (desktop vs mobile)
- [ ] Test VPA table matches implementation exactly
- [ ] Includes a QR embedding code sample

title: Mock bank list endpoint
body:
## Description
Return the list of supported mock banks for the netbanking checkout step.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] At least 8 mock banks with name + logo placeholder
- [ ] Response cacheable (banks rarely change)
- [ ] Centralized bank registry shared with any UI bank-picker component

title: Netbanking redirect page — select bank, approve/cancel
body:
## Description
Hosted page simulating a bank's login + confirm page: pick from the mock bank list, then approve or cancel the payment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No real credentials collected — a single "Approve" / "Cancel" action
- [ ] Page is branded per the selected mock bank for realism
- [ ] Session tied to a single payment, can't be reused for another

title: Netbanking callback handler
body:
## Description
After approve/cancel on the mock bank page, update the Payment and redirect the browser back to the merchant's callback URL.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Callback carries a signed state token verified server-side
- [ ] Idempotent against a replayed callback
- [ ] Redirect URL matches the documented merchant callback contract

title: CSRF/state-token protection on the redirect callback
body:
## Description
The redirect-based flow is a classic CSRF target — generate a per-payment state token at redirect time and require it unchanged on callback.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] State token is cryptographically random, single-use
- [ ] Callback without a valid matching token is rejected, payment untouched
- [ ] Covered by a security-focused test attempting a forged callback

title: Netbanking payment timeout when customer abandons the bank page
body:
## Description
If the customer never approves or cancels, auto-fail the payment after a timeout rather than leaving it pending forever.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Timeout window configurable
- [ ] Reason code distinct from an explicit cancel
- [ ] Covered by a test using a fast-forwarded clock

title: Netbanking refund simulation with bank-side delay
body:
## Description
Implement the netbanking adapter's `Refund`, simulating a longer settlement delay than UPI (closer to the card refund timeline).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Refund starts `pending`, resolves to `processed` after the simulated delay
- [ ] Partial refunds supported
- [ ] Reuses the shared Refund entity

title: Bank-down simulation for merchant error-handling testing
body:
## Description
A special mock bank entry that always returns a "bank unavailable" error, so merchants/integrators can test their own error handling against it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Selecting this bank always fails with a `bank_unavailable` reason code, never succeeds
- [ ] Clearly labeled as a test-only bank in the UI
- [ ] Documented in the netbanking integration guide

title: Netbanking success/failure result UI pages
body:
## Description
Post-redirect landing pages shown briefly before the browser returns to the merchant, confirming the outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Distinct visual states for success, failure, and cancelled
- [ ] Auto-redirects to merchant callback after a short delay
- [ ] Accessible (proper contrast, screen-reader labels)

title: Integration tests for the netbanking redirect flow
body:
## Description
End-to-end test driving the full redirect → mock bank page → callback → merchant-redirect sequence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Covers approve, cancel, and timeout paths
- [ ] Asserts the state-token CSRF guard actually rejects a forged callback
- [ ] Runs in CI

title: Write a netbanking integration guide for merchants
body:
## Description
Developer-portal page explaining the redirect flow, callback contract, and the bank-down test bank.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sequence diagram of the redirect flow included
- [ ] Documents exact query params on the merchant callback
- [ ] Links to the bank-down simulation for error-path testing

title: Mock wallet provider registry
body:
## Description
Define 3-4 fake wallet providers (name, logo placeholder, mock balance store) behind a shared interface, similar to the netbanking bank registry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each mock wallet has an independent fake balance per test customer
- [ ] Registry is centralized, adding a wallet requires one file change
- [ ] Exposed via a `GET /v1/methods/wallets` listing endpoint

title: Wallet balance check mock endpoint
body:
## Description
Before charging, check the mock wallet's balance so insufficient-balance can be simulated realistically.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Returns current mock balance for a given test wallet handle
- [ ] Balance decrements on successful charge, persists across requests within a test session
- [ ] No real money/account involved — clearly a local mock store

title: Wallet OTP authorization step
body:
## Description
Simulate the OTP confirmation step a wallet provider shows before authorizing a charge, reusing the OTP page pattern from Card Payments where reasonable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Correct OTP (non-reserved) approves; reserved fail code declines
- [ ] Attempt count capped same as the card OTP flow
- [ ] Shared OTP UI component reused, not re-implemented

title: Wallet payment authorize + capture flow
body:
## Description
Wire the wallet adapter's Authorize/Capture: balance check → OTP → debit mock balance → capture.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Wallet charges are auto-captured (no manual-capture mode, matching real wallet behavior)
- [ ] Mock balance is only debited after OTP success
- [ ] Failure at any step leaves the mock balance unchanged

title: Simulate insufficient wallet balance
body:
## Description
If the mock wallet balance is below the payment amount, fail before the OTP step with a clear reason code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reason code `insufficient_wallet_balance`, consistent with the Payments core's shared reason-code enum
- [ ] No OTP step is shown when balance is already known to be insufficient
- [ ] Unit tested against a fixed low-balance fixture

title: Wallet refund-to-wallet simulation
body:
## Description
Implement the wallet adapter's `Refund`: credit the mock balance back, resolving faster than card/netbanking refunds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Mock balance is credited back on refund
- [ ] Partial refunds supported
- [ ] Reuses the shared Refund entity

title: Wallet linking/delinking at checkout
body:
## Description
Let a customer link a mock wallet handle to their profile at checkout for faster repeat use, and delink it later.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Linking requires the OTP step once, then is remembered for future checkouts
- [ ] Delinking immediately requires OTP again on next use
- [ ] Mirrors the saved-card consent pattern from Card Payments

title: Surface wallet options on the checkout widget
body:
## Description
List available mock wallets as a payment method tab in the checkout widget, with balance shown once a handle is entered.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Wallet tab only shows wallets enabled for the merchant
- [ ] Shows mock balance after handle entry, before committing to charge
- [ ] Consistent visual pattern with the card/UPI/netbanking tabs

title: Unit tests for the wallet adapter
body:
## Description
Table-driven tests covering balance-check, OTP success/failure, and refund paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Covers sufficient-balance, insufficient-balance, and OTP-failure cases
- [ ] No real network calls — fully in-process against the mock balance store
- [ ] Added to CI

title: Write a wallet integration guide for merchants
body:
## Description
Developer-portal page covering the mock wallet providers, balance-check step, and OTP test codes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Lists all mock wallet providers and their test handles
- [ ] Documents OTP test/fail codes consistent with other methods' docs
- [ ] Cross-linked from the main payment-methods overview page

title: Define PaymentLink data model and migration
body:
## Description
Create the `payment_links` table: amount, currency, description, reference_id, expire_by, status, short_url.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One PaymentLink can generate multiple Payment attempts (same as Orders)
- [ ] status enum: created/paid/partially_paid/expired/cancelled
- [ ] Migration includes an index on short_url for fast public lookup

title: POST /v1/payment_links — create a payment link
body:
## Description
Authenticated endpoint for a merchant to generate a payment link without needing an Order created up front.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Internally creates a backing Order the link points to
- [ ] Accepts optional customer notify flags (email/sms) consumed by the Notifications epic
- [ ] Returns the full public short_url in the response

title: Hosted payment link page — public, no API key required
body:
## Description
The page a customer lands on when visiting the short URL: shows amount/description and the standard method tabs (card/UPI/netbanking/wallet).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No authentication required to view or pay
- [ ] Reuses the checkout widget's method tabs rather than duplicating payment UI
- [ ] Shows "expired"/"already paid" states appropriately instead of a payment form

title: Short URL generation for payment links
body:
## Description
Generate a compact, non-sequential short code for the public link path (avoid guessable/sequential IDs leaking link existence/order).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Short code is URL-safe and collision-checked on generation
- [ ] Not derived from the link's numeric/sequential primary key
- [ ] Length balances brevity and guess-resistance

title: Payment link expiry handling
body:
## Description
Honor `expire_by` — once passed, the public page shows an expired state and rejects further payment attempts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Expiry checked both client-side (immediate UX) and server-side (authoritative)
- [ ] A payment that was in-flight right at expiry is still settled correctly (no ledger issue)
- [ ] Covered by a boundary test at the exact expiry instant

title: Payment link reminder notifications
body:
## Description
Allow a merchant to trigger a reminder (email/SMS) for an unpaid payment link, reusing the Notifications epic's delivery channel.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reminder only sendable for links in `created`/`partially_paid` status
- [ ] Rate-limited to prevent reminder spam to the same customer
- [ ] Reminder content includes the same short_url

title: Support partial payments on a payment link
body:
## Description
Allow a payment link to accept partial payments toward its total, building on the Payments core's partial-payment support.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Merchant opts in per-link (`partial_payment: true`)
- [ ] Minimum partial amount configurable
