- [ ] Link status reflects `partially_paid` distinctly from fully `paid`

title: Cancel/deactivate a payment link
body:
## Description
Let a merchant cancel an active, unpaid payment link via the API and dashboard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cancelled links immediately reject new payment attempts
- [ ] Cannot cancel a link that's already fully paid
- [ ] Status change is audit-logged

title: GET /v1/payment_links — list and filter payment links
body:
## Description
List endpoint mirroring Orders' list semantics, filterable by status and date range.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pagination consistent with other list endpoints
- [ ] Includes amount_paid progress for partial-payment links
- [ ] Covered by an integration test

title: Dashboard UI: create and manage payment links
body:
## Description
A dedicated dashboard section for generating a link, copying its short URL, viewing status, and cancelling/reminding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One-click copy of the short URL
- [ ] Status badge matches the link's current state
- [ ] Reminder and cancel actions available inline from the list view

title: Design embeddable checkout widget API (open/close/callbacks)
body:
## Description
Define the public JS API surface for the PayGate checkout widget: how a merchant's page instantiates it, opens/closes it, and receives success/failure/dismiss callbacks. This is the contract every later widget screen builds against.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Public API documented: `PayGate.checkout({ key, order_id, handler, modal: { ondismiss } })`
- [ ] `.open()` / `.close()` methods defined
- [ ] Success callback receives payment_id + signature for server-side verification
- [ ] Failure callback receives an error code/description
- [ ] API design reviewed against docs/ARCHITECTURE.md API principles

title: Build widget bootstrap/loader script (paygate-checkout.js)
body:
## Description
Build the small loader script merchants embed via `<script src="paygate-checkout.js">` that lazily injects the full widget bundle in an iframe/modal, keeping the merchant page's load time unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Loader script is < 5KB and has no external dependencies
- [ ] Injects widget iframe only when `.open()` is called
- [ ] Widget origin is isolated from merchant page (postMessage bridge)
- [ ] Works when included multiple times on the same page without duplicate init

title: Render payment method selection screen in widget
body:
## Description
First screen inside the widget: list available payment methods (Cards, UPI, Netbanking, Wallets) for the merchant/order, and route to the right method-specific screen on selection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Method list is driven by merchant's enabled methods, not hardcoded
- [ ] Selecting a method transitions to that method's entry screen
- [ ] Back navigation returns to method selection
- [ ] Screen matches order amount/currency display

title: Implement card entry form with client-side validation
body:
## Description
Build the card number/expiry/CVV entry screen with client-side Luhn and expiry validation before submitting to the Payments API, to avoid round-tripping obviously invalid input.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Card number formatted with spacing as typed, Luhn-validated
- [ ] Expiry and CVV format/length validated client-side
- [ ] Card network icon detected and shown from BIN prefix
- [ ] Submits to Payments API only once per click (prevents double-submit)
- [ ] Raw card data never logged client-side

title: Implement UPI VPA entry screen in widget
body:
## Description
Build the UPI Collect entry screen: customer enters a VPA (e.g. `name@bank`), widget validates format client-side and submits a Collect request, then polls for approval status.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] VPA format validated client-side before submit
- [ ] Screen shows "waiting for approval on your UPI app" state while polling
- [ ] Handles approve/decline/timeout outcomes distinctly
- [ ] Option to switch to UPI Intent (deep link) instead of Collect

title: Implement netbanking bank-selection screen in widget
body:
## Description
Build the netbanking screen: searchable list of mock banks, selecting one redirects (within the widget) to the mock bank's approve/cancel page.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bank list is searchable/filterable
- [ ] Popular banks shown first
- [ ] Redirect to mock bank page carries a signed reference back to the Payment
- [ ] Cancel on the mock bank page returns the widget to method selection with a failed state

title: Implement wallet selection screen in widget
body:
## Description
Build the wallet payment screen: list mock wallet providers, selecting one simulates a balance check and OTP step before confirming the payment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Wallet provider list rendered from merchant's enabled wallets
- [ ] Mock OTP step with a 6-digit input
- [ ] Insufficient-balance outcome handled distinctly from OTP failure
- [ ] Successful confirm returns to widget's success state

title: Wire widget to create and poll Payment via Payments API
body:
## Description
Connect every method screen to the real backend flow: create the Payment against the Order, then poll `GET /v1/payments/:id` until a terminal state is reached, driving the widget's success/failure callbacks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Widget never calls payment-processing endpoints with the merchant's secret key (public key only)
- [ ] Polling has a sane interval and max duration, then times out gracefully
- [ ] Terminal states (captured/failed) map correctly to widget callbacks
- [ ] Idempotency-Key reused across a given attempt's retries

title: Add widget theming/customization (logo, color, merchant name)
body:
## Description
Let merchants pass branding options (logo URL, primary color, display name) into the widget init call so checkout looks like part of their site rather than a generic PayGate screen.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `theme: { color, logo }` accepted in widget init options
- [ ] Falls back to PayGate default branding when omitted
- [ ] Logo URL is validated/sanitized before rendering
- [ ] Color contrast checked against a minimum accessibility threshold

title: Build hosted payment page (non-widget checkout URL)
body:
## Description
Some integrations can't embed JS (e.g. an email link). Build a standalone hosted checkout page at a PayGate URL that offers the same payment methods without requiring the merchant to embed anything.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `GET /checkout/:order_id` renders a full-page checkout for that order
- [ ] Shares method-screen components with the embedded widget (no duplicated logic)
- [ ] Redirects to a merchant-configured return URL on completion
- [ ] Expired/invalid order IDs show a clear error page

title: Add widget cross-browser/responsive test suite
body:
## Description
Automated tests covering the widget across common viewport sizes and the last two versions of major browsers, since checkout is the most visible, highest-stakes UI in the product.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test suite runs against Chrome, Firefox, Safari (latest two versions)
- [ ] Mobile viewport layout covered (iframe sizing, keyboard overlap)
- [ ] Visual regression snapshots for each method screen
- [ ] Suite runs in CI on every PR touching `frontend/checkout-widget`

title: Write checkout widget integration guide
body:
## Description
Developer-facing guide for integrating the checkout widget: script tag, init options, handling callbacks, and server-side payment verification — modeled on the clarity of Razorpay's own integration docs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Copy-pasteable quickstart snippet
- [ ] Full options reference table
- [ ] Server-side signature verification example included
- [ ] Common integration mistakes called out (e.g. verifying on client only)

title: Design Plan, Subscription, and Mandate schema
body:
## Description
Define the data model for recurring billing: a `Plan` (amount, interval, interval count), a `Subscription` (customer bound to a plan, current cycle, status), and a `Mandate` (the customer's one-time authorization for future auto-debits).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Schema supports daily/weekly/monthly/yearly intervals with a count (e.g. every 3 months)
- [ ] Subscription status enum covers created/active/paused/cancelled/completed
- [ ] Mandate stores authorization method and max-amount-per-charge
- [ ] Migration reviewed against docs/ARCHITECTURE.md domain model

title: POST /v1/plans — create billing plan
body:
## Description
API for a merchant to define a reusable billing plan (amount, interval, name) that subscriptions are created against.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Validates amount > 0 and a supported interval
- [ ] Returns the created plan with a `plan_id`
- [ ] Idempotency-Key supported
- [ ] Scoped to the authenticated merchant and test/live mode

title: GET /v1/plans and GET /v1/plans/:id
body:
## Description
Read APIs for listing and fetching a merchant's billing plans, used by both the dashboard UI and merchant integrations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] List endpoint supports pagination
- [ ] Fetch-by-id returns 404 for plans outside the caller's merchant scope
- [ ] Response shape matches the plan object returned by POST /v1/plans

title: POST /v1/subscriptions — create subscription for a customer+plan
body:
## Description
Bind a customer to a plan, creating a Subscription in `created` status pending mandate authorization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Requires a valid plan_id and customer reference
- [ ] Rejects if plan belongs to a different merchant
- [ ] Returns subscription with a short_url for the customer to authorize the mandate
- [ ] Idempotency-Key supported

title: Implement mandate authorization flow (customer one-time approval)
body:
## Description
Customer-facing flow where the customer approves the recurring mandate once (via the checkout widget), after which the subscription becomes `active` and future charges need no further customer action.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Mandate authorization reuses checkout widget payment-method screens
- [ ] On approval, Subscription transitions created → active
- [ ] Mandate records max-amount-per-charge and expiry
- [ ] Declined authorization leaves subscription in a distinct failed/created state, not silently active

title: Build recurring charge scheduler worker
body:
## Description
Background worker that, on each subscription's billing cycle boundary, creates a Payment against the stored mandate without customer interaction.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Scheduler is idempotent per (subscription_id, cycle) — never double-charges a cycle
- [ ] Runs as a separate worker process from the API, per repo structure in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- [ ] Charge amount and timing match the plan's interval
- [ ] Scheduler failures are logged and retryable without side effects

title: Implement retry logic for failed recurring charges (dunning)
body:
## Description
When a scheduled recurring charge fails (e.g. simulated insufficient funds), retry on a backoff schedule before marking the subscription past-due or cancelled.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Configurable retry schedule (e.g. day 1, 3, 7 after failure)
- [ ] Subscription enters a `past_due` status during retries
- [ ] Subscription auto-cancels after exhausting retries, per plan config
- [ ] Each retry attempt is visible in the subscription's charge history

title: POST /v1/subscriptions/:id/cancel
body:
## Description
Allow a merchant to cancel a subscription immediately or at the end of the current cycle.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Supports `cancel_at_cycle_end: true|false`
- [ ] Cancelled subscription stops being picked up by the scheduler
- [ ] Returns updated subscription status
- [ ] Emits a cancellation event for the webhook dispatcher

title: POST /v1/subscriptions/:id/pause and /resume
body:
## Description
Allow temporarily pausing billing (e.g. customer on hold) without cancelling the mandate, and resuming later.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Paused subscriptions are skipped by the scheduler
- [ ] Resume recalculates the next charge date correctly
- [ ] Pause/resume actions are recorded in subscription history

title: Emit subscription.charged / subscription.cancelled webhook events
body:
## Description
Hook the subscription scheduler and cancellation/pause actions into the webhook event system so merchants can react to billing lifecycle changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] subscription.charged fired on each successful recurring charge
- [ ] subscription.cancelled fired on cancellation (manual or dunning exhaustion)
- [ ] Events carry subscription_id, plan_id, and payment_id where applicable
- [ ] Covered by the webhook delivery/retry mechanism from the Webhooks epic

title: Add subscription management UI in merchant dashboard
body:
## Description
Dashboard screens for merchants to view active subscriptions, their status/history, and trigger pause/resume/cancel actions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] List view with status filter (active/past_due/cancelled)
- [ ] Detail view shows charge history and next billing date
- [ ] Pause/resume/cancel actions wired to the Subscriptions API
- [ ] Matches dashboard design conventions used elsewhere in the app

title: Add subscription list/detail view in admin panel
body:
## Description
Internal ops view across all merchants' subscriptions, for support/debugging billing issues.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Searchable by merchant, customer reference, or subscription_id
- [ ] Shows mandate status and recent scheduler runs for a subscription
- [ ] Read-only (no destructive actions from admin panel in this epic)

title: Write integration tests for recurring billing lifecycle
body:
## Description
End-to-end tests covering plan creation → subscription creation → mandate authorization → scheduled charge → dunning retry → cancellation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Scheduler can be run with a mocked clock to simulate multiple cycles quickly
- [ ] Covers the failed-charge-then-dunning-then-cancel path
- [ ] Asserts no double-charge occurs if the scheduler runs twice for the same cycle

title: Write subscriptions API documentation
body:
## Description
Developer docs for Plans, Subscriptions, and Mandates: endpoints, lifecycle diagram, and webhook events.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Lifecycle diagram matches the actual status enum in code
- [ ] Every endpoint has a request/response example
- [ ] Dunning/retry behavior documented so merchants know what to expect

title: Design Refund entity and state machine
body:
## Description
Define the Refund data model and its states (pending, processed, failed), linked to the originating captured Payment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Refund references the source payment_id and amount
- [ ] State transitions match docs/ARCHITECTURE.md payment state machine conventions
- [ ] A Payment tracks total refunded amount to prevent over-refunding

title: POST /v1/payments/:id/refund — full refund
body:
## Description
API to refund the entire captured amount of a Payment back to the original method.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Only allowed on payments in `captured` state
- [ ] Rejects refunding an already fully-refunded payment
- [ ] Returns the created Refund object with `pending` status
- [ ] Transitions Payment to `refunded` once processed

title: Support partial refund amount in refund API
body:
## Description
Allow refunding less than the full captured amount, including multiple partial refunds against the same payment up to the captured total.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `amount` field accepted and validated against remaining refundable balance
- [ ] Multiple partial refunds against one payment are supported
- [ ] Payment status reflects partial vs full refund distinctly if the API models that

title: Post ledger journal entries for refund reversal
body:
## Description
Every processed refund must post balanced double-entry journal entries that reverse the original capture's effect on the merchant's and customer suspense accounts, per the ledger model in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Journal entries for a refund sum to zero
- [ ] merchant_payable account is debited by the refunded amount
- [ ] Refund fee handling (if any) is a separate, explicit journal entry, not folded silently into the refund amount
- [ ] Ledger balance view reflects the refund immediately after processing

title: Enforce refund idempotency via Idempotency-Key
body:
## Description
Prevent duplicate refunds caused by client retries by requiring and honoring the Idempotency-Key header on the refund endpoint.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Same key + same body returns the original Refund, no new ledger entries
- [ ] Same key + different body returns a 409/conflict error
- [ ] Idempotency keys expire after a defined window (e.g. 24h)

title: Implement refund speed tiers (normal vs instant simulation)
body:
## Description
Simulate Razorpay-style refund speed options: a default multi-day refund vs. an instant refund tier with a higher simulated fee.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `speed: normal|instant` accepted on the refund request
- [ ] Instant refunds simulate immediate settlement-to-customer with an extra fee journal entry
- [ ] Normal refunds simulate a processing delay before reaching `processed` state

title: Emit refund.created / refund.processed webhook events
body:
## Description
Hook refund creation and completion into the webhook event system.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] refund.created fired synchronously on API response
- [ ] refund.processed fired once the refund reaches a terminal state
- [ ] Event payload includes refund_id, payment_id, and amount

title: Add refunds list/detail UI in merchant dashboard
body:
## Description
Dashboard screens to view refunds against a payment and initiate new full/partial refunds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Refund action available from a payment's detail view
- [ ] Partial refund amount input validated against remaining refundable balance before submit
- [ ] Refund status and speed tier shown in the list view

title: Write unit tests for refund ledger correctness
body:
## Description
Tests asserting that every refund scenario (full, partial, instant, repeated partials) produces journal entries that sum to zero and leave the ledger in a correct, auditable state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Covers full refund, partial refund, and multiple-partials-to-full scenarios
- [ ] Asserts over-refund attempts are rejected before touching the ledger
- [ ] Asserts fee entries are isolated from principal refund entries

title: Write refunds API documentation
body:
## Description
Developer docs covering the refund endpoint, partial refund semantics, speed tiers, and related webhook events.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Request/response examples for full and partial refunds
- [ ] Speed tier fee implications documented
- [ ] Idempotency behavior documented

title: Design Dispute entity and lifecycle
body:
## Description
Define the Dispute data model and status flow (open → under_review → won/lost), linked to a captured Payment, matching the dispute lifecycle described in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dispute references source payment_id, reason code, and amount under dispute
- [ ] Status enum covers open/under_review/won/lost
- [ ] Schema supports a deadline field for evidence submission

title: Build internal API to raise a dispute against a captured payment
body:
## Description
Since PayGate has no real card network, disputes are raised via an internal/admin-triggered API that simulates a chargeback arriving from the network, so the rest of the dispute flow can be exercised.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Only callable on `captured` or `settled` payments
- [ ] Creates a Dispute in `open` status with a deadline
- [ ] Holds the disputed amount in a suspense ledger account immediately
- [ ] Not exposed on the public merchant-facing API surface

title: POST /v1/disputes/:id/evidence — submit evidence documents
body:
## Description
Let the merchant submit evidence (text explanation + file attachments) to contest an open dispute before its deadline.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rejects submissions after the deadline
- [ ] Supports multiple evidence attachments per submission
- [ ] Transitions dispute to `under_review` on successful submission
- [ ] Stores submission timestamp for audit purposes

title: Implement dispute deadline tracking and reminders
body:
## Description
Track each open dispute's evidence deadline and trigger reminder notifications as it approaches, so merchants don't lose disputes by default through inaction.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reminder sent at a configurable interval before deadline (e.g. 3 days, 1 day)
- [ ] Disputes past deadline with no evidence auto-resolve to `lost`
- [ ] Reminder job is idempotent (doesn't double-send on worker restart)

title: Implement dispute resolution and ledger adjustment on loss
body:
## Description
Admin-driven (simulating network) resolution of a dispute to won or lost, with the correct ledger effect: won releases the held suspense amount back to the merchant, lost debits the merchant permanently.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Resolution to `won` releases suspense-held funds back to merchant_payable
- [ ] Resolution to `lost` posts a permanent debit against merchant_payable plus any dispute fee
- [ ] Resolution is a one-way transition (no re-resolving a closed dispute)
- [ ] Ledger entries for each outcome sum to zero

title: Hold disputed payment amount in a suspense ledger account
body:
## Description
When a dispute is opened, immediately move the disputed amount into a `customer_suspense`-style holding account so the merchant's available balance correctly reflects funds at risk.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hold happens atomically with dispute creation
- [ ] Merchant's computed available balance excludes held amounts
- [ ] Held amount is clearly attributable to its dispute_id for reconciliation

title: Emit dispute.created / dispute.won / dispute.lost webhook events
body:
## Description
Hook dispute creation and resolution into the webhook event system so merchants can automate their own response workflows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each lifecycle transition emits a distinct event
- [ ] Event payload includes dispute_id, payment_id, amount, and deadline (for dispute.created)
- [ ] Covered by standard webhook retry/signature mechanism

title: Add disputes list/detail UI with evidence upload in merchant dashboard
body:
## Description
Dashboard screens for merchants to see open disputes, their deadlines, and submit evidence directly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] List view highlights disputes nearing deadline
- [ ] Detail view supports file upload for evidence
- [ ] Resolved disputes show final outcome and ledger impact

title: Add dispute review queue in admin panel
body:
## Description
Internal ops screen to review submitted evidence and resolve disputes to won/lost, simulating the role a real network/issuer would play.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Queue lists disputes in `under_review` with submitted evidence visible
- [ ] Resolve action wired to the resolution API and its ledger effects
- [ ] Action is audit-logged with the admin user who resolved it

title: Write integration tests for dispute-to-ledger-adjustment flow
body:
## Description
Tests covering the full path from dispute creation through evidence submission to both won and lost resolutions, asserting correct ledger state at each step.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Covers won path (funds released) and lost path (funds debited)
- [ ] Covers auto-lost-on-deadline-expiry path
- [ ] Asserts merchant available balance is correct after each outcome

title: Write dispute evidence submission documentation
body:
## Description
Merchant-facing docs explaining the dispute lifecycle, deadlines, what evidence to submit, and the ledger impact of each outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Lifecycle diagram included
- [ ] Evidence submission endpoint documented with examples
- [ ] Clearly states consequences of missing the deadline

title: Add email notification on new dispute raised
body:
## Description
Notify the merchant by email as soon as a dispute is opened against one of their payments, since disputes are time-sensitive.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Email includes payment_id, amount, reason, and deadline
- [ ] Sent via the notification service built in the Notifications epic
- [ ] Failure to send is logged but doesn't block dispute creation

title: Design Settlement and Payout entities and schedule model
body:
## Description
Define the data model for Settlements (batches of captured payments moved to a merchant's bank) and Payouts (merchant-initiated outbound transfers), plus supported schedules (T+2, daily, weekly).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Settlement references the set of payment_ids included and total/fee/net amounts
- [ ] Merchant has a configurable settlement schedule field
- [ ] Payout is modeled as distinct from Settlement per docs/ARCHITECTURE.md domain model

title: Build settlement batching job
body:
## Description
Scheduled worker that groups each merchant's eligible captured payments (past any hold period) into a Settlement batch according to their configured schedule.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Batching respects each merchant's individual schedule
- [ ] A payment is included in exactly one settlement batch, never duplicated
- [ ] Batching is restartable/idempotent if the worker crashes mid-run

title: Implement fee calculation and deduction (MDR, GST) per transaction
body:
## Description
Compute PayGate's merchant discount rate (MDR) fee and simulated GST on that fee for every captured payment, deducted at settlement time.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Fee rate configurable per merchant or payment method
- [ ] GST computed as a percentage of the MDR fee, not of the transaction amount
- [ ] Fee and GST appear as separate, explicit ledger entries
- [ ] Net settled amount = captured amount − MDR − GST, reconcilable line by line

title: Post settlement ledger entries (merchant_payable → settlement_clearing)
body:
## Description
When a settlement batch is created, post the corresponding journal entries moving funds from each merchant's payable account into a settlement clearing account pending bank transfer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Entries posted atomically with batch creation
- [ ] Clearing account balance matches the sum of all pending settlement batches
- [ ] Entries are traceable back to the specific settlement_id

title: Simulate bank payout transfer (mock UTR generation)
body:
## Description
Simulate the final leg of settlement — transferring funds from clearing to the merchant's registered bank account — generating a mock UTR (transaction reference) as a real bank would.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Mock transfer has a simulated processing delay before marking `processed`
- [ ] A unique mock UTR is generated and stored per settlement
- [ ] Clearing account is debited and a simulated "bank" account credited on completion

title: Handle settlement failure/retry (invalid bank account simulation)
body:
## Description
Simulate real-world settlement failures (e.g. invalid/closed bank account) and the retry/hold workflow that follows, rather than assuming every payout always succeeds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Failed settlement reverses the clearing-account debit back to merchant_payable
- [ ] Merchant is notified and prompted to update bank details
- [ ] Failed settlements are retried automatically once bank details are corrected

title: POST /v1/payouts — merchant-initiated vendor payout
body:
## Description
Allow a merchant to initiate an outbound payout to a third-party bank account/VPA (e.g. paying a vendor), separate from their own settlement flow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Validates sufficient available merchant balance before initiating
- [ ] Supports bank account and UPI VPA as payout destinations
- [ ] Posts ledger entries debiting merchant_payable on initiation
- [ ] Idempotency-Key supported

title: Support on-demand instant settlement (extra fee)
body:
## Description
Let a merchant pull an early settlement outside their normal schedule for a higher simulated fee, mirroring Razorpay's "Instant Settlements" feature.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Instant settlement fee rate is distinct from and higher than standard MDR
- [ ] Only eligible (captured, hold-period-cleared) payments can be instant-settled
- [ ] Instant settlement skips the normal batching schedule for just that payment set

title: Emit settlement.processed / payout.processed webhook events
body:
## Description
Hook settlement and payout completion into the webhook event system.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] settlement.processed includes UTR, net amount, and included payment count
- [ ] payout.processed includes payout_id, destination, and status
- [ ] Failure outcomes also emit a distinct failed event

title: Add settlements list/detail UI with downloadable UTR report
body:
## Description
Dashboard screens showing settlement history per merchant, with a downloadable report (CSV) of included transactions and fees for a given settlement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] List view shows settlement date, gross, fees, net, and UTR
- [ ] Detail view lists every payment included in that settlement
- [ ] CSV export matches the on-screen totals exactly

title: Add payouts UI in merchant dashboard
body:
## Description
Dashboard screens to initiate and track vendor payouts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Form to initiate a payout with destination and amount
- [ ] List view of past payouts with status
- [ ] Insufficient-balance case shows a clear inline error before submit

title: Add settlement schedule configuration UI in admin panel
body:
## Description
Internal tool for ops to configure or override a merchant's settlement schedule (e.g. moving a merchant from T+2 to weekly).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Schedule change takes effect from the next batching run, not retroactively
- [ ] Change is audit-logged with the admin user and timestamp
- [ ] Shows the merchant's current and pending-next schedule

title: Write reconciliation unit tests for settlement batch totals
body:
## Description
Tests asserting that for any settlement batch, gross − MDR − GST = net, and that the sum of ledger entries for the batch is zero.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Covers batches with mixed payment methods and fee rates
- [ ] Covers the instant-settlement fee path
- [ ] Fails loudly (not silently rounds) on any penny-level mismatch

title: Write settlements & payouts documentation
body:
## Description
Merchant-facing docs explaining settlement schedules, fee structure, instant settlement, and payouts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Fee calculation example walked through numerically
- [ ] Schedule options and how to change them documented
- [ ] Payout destinations and limits documented

title: Design domain event schema and internal event bus
body:
## Description
Define a consistent internal event envelope (event type, resource payload, timestamp, merchant_id) and the internal bus/queue that ledger and service-layer writes publish to, which the webhook dispatcher and settlement engine both consume, per the event-driven design in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Event envelope schema documented and versioned
- [ ] Publishing an event is decoupled from any single consumer failing
- [ ] At-least-once delivery semantics to internal consumers

title: Build webhook endpoint registration API (CRUD)
body:
## Description
API/dashboard-backing endpoints for a merchant to register, update, and remove webhook endpoint URLs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Validates the URL is HTTPS before accepting it
- [ ] Supports multiple endpoints per merchant
- [ ] Returns a signing secret on creation, never re-displayed in full afterward

title: Implement per-merchant event subscription
body:
## Description
Let each registered endpoint subscribe to a specific subset of event types (e.g. only payment.captured and refund.processed) instead of receiving everything.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Endpoint config stores a list of subscribed event types
- [ ] Dispatcher filters events per-endpoint before attempting delivery
- [ ] Dashboard UI lists all available event types to subscribe to

title: Implement HMAC-SHA256 request signing (X-PayGate-Signature)
body:
## Description
Sign every outbound webhook payload with HMAC-SHA256 using the endpoint's secret, sent in the `X-PayGate-Signature` header, so merchants can verify authenticity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Signature computed over the raw request body, not a re-serialized copy
- [ ] Secret rotation supported without breaking in-flight deliveries
- [ ] Verification reference implementation matches what's documented for merchants

title: Build webhook delivery worker with exponential backoff retry
body:
## Description
Worker that delivers queued webhook events to merchant endpoints, retrying failed deliveries (non-2xx or timeout) with exponential backoff up to a max attempt count.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Backoff schedule is configurable (base delay, multiplier, max attempts)
- [ ] A slow/down endpoint doesn't block delivery to other merchants' endpoints
- [ ] Delivery timeout is enforced so one bad endpoint can't hang a worker indefinitely

title: Log every webhook delivery attempt
body:
## Description
Persist a delivery log entry (status, HTTP response code, latency, attempt number) for every delivery attempt, successful or not, for debuggability and the dashboard's delivery history view.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Log includes request and response bodies (truncated if oversized)
- [ ] Log is queryable by event_id and by endpoint_id
- [ ] Retained for a defined retention window

title: Build manual webhook redelivery action in dashboard
body:
## Description
Let a merchant manually trigger redelivery of a specific past event to a specific endpoint from the dashboard, useful after fixing a bug on their receiving server.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Redelivery creates a new delivery attempt record, doesn't mutate history
- [ ] Redelivery uses the current signing secret, not the one at original send time
- [ ] Rate-limited to prevent abuse

title: Add webhook signature verification code sample
body:
## Description
Publish a reference code sample (e.g. Node and Go) merchants can copy to verify the X-PayGate-Signature header on their receiving endpoint.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sample correctly rejects a tampered payload
- [ ] Sample matches the exact signing scheme implemented server-side
- [ ] Included directly in the webhooks documentation page

title: Implement dead-letter handling after max retry attempts
body:
## Description
When a webhook delivery exhausts all retry attempts, move it to a dead-letter state instead of retrying forever, and surface it clearly to the merchant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dead-lettered deliveries are visible and filterable in the dashboard
- [ ] Merchant is notified when an endpoint accumulates repeated dead-letters (likely broken endpoint)
- [ ] Dead-lettered events remain manually redeliverable

title: Add webhooks configuration UI in merchant dashboard
body:
## Description
Dashboard screens to manage endpoints, subscriptions, view the signing secret (once, on creation), and browse delivery history.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Endpoint CRUD wired to the registration API
- [ ] Event type subscription picker
- [ ] Delivery history view with status, latency, and retry/redeliver actions

title: Write integration tests for signature verification and retry backoff
body:
## Description
Tests covering correct signature generation/verification and the retry backoff schedule under simulated endpoint failure and recovery.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Asserts tampered payloads fail verification
- [ ] Asserts backoff delays match the configured schedule within tolerance
- [ ] Asserts dead-letter triggers only after the configured max attempts

title: Add webhook event catalog documentation
body:
## Description
Reference page listing every event type PayGate emits, its payload shape, and which domain action triggers it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every event type implemented in code appears in the catalog (kept in sync)
- [ ] Each entry has a sample payload
- [ ] Grouped by module (payments, refunds, disputes, settlements, subscriptions)

title: Design rule-based risk scoring model
body:
## Description
Define a composable risk scoring model where individual rules each contribute a score (0-100 scale) and the engine combines them into an overall risk score per payment attempt.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each rule is independently pluggable/testable
- [ ] Overall score combination method is deterministic and documented
- [ ] Score and contributing rule breakdown are stored against the payment for audit

title: Implement velocity check rule
body:
## Description
Flag payment attempts when the same card/VPA/IP has made an unusually high number of attempts within a short time window, a classic fraud/testing signal.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Configurable window size and attempt threshold
- [ ] Tracks per-card, per-VPA, and per-IP independently
- [ ] Rule contributes a proportional (not binary) score, not just pass/fail

title: Implement amount-anomaly rule
body:
## Description
Flag payments that are unusually large relative to a merchant's historical average transaction size, since a sudden large transaction is a common fraud pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Baseline computed from a rolling window of the merchant's recent captured payments
- [ ] New merchants with insufficient history are handled with a sane default, not a false-positive flood
- [ ] Rule score scales with how far the amount deviates from baseline

title: Implement mismatched geolocation/IP risk rule
body:
## Description
Using a mock IP-geolocation lookup, flag payments where the customer's apparent location is inconsistent with their stated billing details or prior activity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] IP geolocation is mocked (no real external lookup), returning deterministic test data
- [ ] Rule contributes a moderate, not dominant, weight to the overall score
- [ ] Documented clearly as simulated, since this is the easiest rule to misread as "real"

title: Build manual review queue for high-risk payments
body:
## Description
Payments scoring above a threshold are held in a pending-review state (not auto-captured/auto-failed) until manually approved or blocked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Threshold is configurable
- [ ] Held payments don't silently time out — they surface clearly in the review queue
- [ ] Review queue entries include the risk score breakdown by rule

title: Add admin action to approve/block a flagged payment
body:
## Description
Admin-panel action to resolve a held payment: approve (proceed to capture) or block (fail permanently), from the fraud review queue.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Approve transitions the payment into the normal capture flow
- [ ] Block transitions the payment to failed with a fraud-specific failure reason
- [ ] Action is audit-logged with the admin user

title: Implement merchant-level risk rule configuration
body:
## Description
Allow per-merchant tuning of risk thresholds (e.g. a merchant with high legitimate transaction variance can raise their amount-anomaly threshold).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Per-merchant overrides fall back to sane platform defaults when unset
- [ ] Only exposed via admin panel in this phase (not self-service)
- [ ] Config changes apply to new payment attempts only, not retroactively

title: Emit payment.flagged webhook event
body:
## Description
Notify merchants via webhook when one of their payments is held for manual fraud review.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Event fires when a payment enters the review queue, not on every score calculation
- [ ] Payload includes payment_id and a generic risk reason (no internal rule internals leaked)
- [ ] Covered by standard webhook delivery/retry

title: Add blocklist management (cards/VPAs/IPs) in admin panel
body:
## Description
Let ops maintain a blocklist of known-bad cards (by token/fingerprint), VPAs, and IPs that are auto-blocked at authorization time regardless of score.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Blocklist entries support add/remove with a reason and audit trail
- [ ] Blocked identifiers are rejected before any other risk scoring runs (cheap short-circuit)
- [ ] Search/filter in the admin UI

title: Add fraud review queue UI in admin panel
body:
## Description
Internal screen listing all payments currently held for review, with their score breakdown and one-click approve/block actions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Queue sortable by score/age
- [ ] Score breakdown shown per contributing rule
- [ ] Approve/block actions wired to the resolution API

title: Write unit tests for each risk rule in isolation
body:
## Description
Each risk rule should be independently testable with synthetic inputs, decoupled from the full payment pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Velocity, amount-anomaly, and geolocation rules each have dedicated test files
- [ ] Tests cover boundary conditions (exactly at threshold)
- [ ] Tests don't depend on wall-clock time (use an injectable clock)

title: Write fraud engine rule documentation
body:
## Description
Internal documentation describing each risk rule, its inputs, scoring contribution, and configuration knobs — for future contributors adding new rules.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One section per rule with a worked scoring example
- [ ] Documents how to add a new rule to the engine
- [ ] Explicitly notes which signals are simulated vs. would need real data in production

title: Integrate mock transactional email provider
body:
## Description
Add an email-sending abstraction (`notifications/email`) backed by a mock SMTP/sandbox provider so the service can send transactional emails without a real provider account. Must support templated HTML emails and a sandbox mode that logs instead of sending in dev.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `EmailSender` interface with a mock/sandbox implementation
- [ ] Supports HTML templates with variable substitution
- [ ] Sandbox mode writes sent emails to a local outbox (DB table or file) for inspection
- [ ] Retries transient send failures with backoff
- [ ] Unit tests for template rendering and retry behavior

title: Integrate mock SMS gateway
body:
## Description
Add an `SmsSender` abstraction backed by a mock SMS gateway for OTP and transactional alerts (e.g. dispute raised). Mirrors the email sender's sandbox-mode design.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `SmsSender` interface with mock implementation
- [ ] Sandbox mode logs sent SMS to an outbox table
- [ ] Phone number format validation (E.164, India +91)
- [ ] Unit tests covering invalid numbers and send failures

title: Send payment captured email to merchant
body:
## Description
When a Payment transitions to `captured`, send the merchant's account email a notification with payment amount, order id, and method. Triggered off the domain event emitted by the ledger write, not a direct call from the payment handler.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Listens to `payment.captured` event
- [ ] Email includes amount, currency, order id, payment method, timestamp
- [ ] Respects merchant notification preferences (see preferences issue)
- [ ] Integration test: captured payment triggers exactly one email

title: Send payment failed email to merchant
body:
## Description
Notify the merchant when a Payment transitions to `failed`, including the failure reason code so they can see why without opening the dashboard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Listens to `payment.failed` event
- [ ] Email includes failure reason/code and order id
- [ ] Does not fire for test-mode payments unless merchant opts in
- [ ] Integration test for the failure path

title: Send settlement completed email to merchant
body:
## Description
When a Settlement batch completes, email the merchant a summary: total settled amount, fee deducted, number of payments included, and a link to the settlement detail page.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Listens to `settlement.completed` event
- [ ] Email includes settlement id, net amount, fee total, payment count
- [ ] Link to dashboard settlement detail page
- [ ] Integration test verifying email content matches settlement record

title: Send dispute raised notification (email + SMS)
body:
## Description
When a Dispute is created against one of a merchant's payments, notify them via both email and SMS given the time-sensitivity of dispute evidence deadlines.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Listens to `dispute.created` event
- [ ] Sends both email and SMS (SMS only if phone verified)
- [ ] Message includes evidence submission deadline
- [ ] Integration test for dual-channel delivery

title: Send customer payment receipt email
body:
## Description
On successful payment capture, optionally email the customer (not the merchant) a receipt if an email address was captured during checkout. Controlled by a merchant-level setting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Customer email only sent if merchant has enabled receipts and an email was collected
- [ ] Receipt includes merchant name, amount, date, payment id (no sensitive card data)
- [ ] Unit test for the opt-in/opt-out branching

title: Notification preferences settings per merchant
body:
## Description
Let merchants choose which events trigger email/SMS notifications (e.g. disable payment-failed emails, keep settlement emails on). Backs the dashboard notification settings page.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `notification_preferences` table keyed by merchant_id + event_type + channel
- [ ] API to read/update preferences
- [ ] Notification senders check preferences before sending
- [ ] Sensible defaults for a newly onboarded merchant

title: Dashboard shell: navigation, auth guard, test/live mode toggle
body:
## Description
Build the dashboard's app shell: sidebar navigation, route guards that redirect unauthenticated users to login, and a persistent test/live mode toggle that scopes all subsequent API calls to the selected mode's API key.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sidebar nav with routes for Payments, Orders, Refunds, Settlements, Payment Links, Subscriptions, Webhooks, Settings
- [ ] Route guard redirects to /login when session is missing/expired
- [ ] Test/live toggle persists across reloads and is visually distinct (banner color)
- [ ] All data-fetching hooks read the current mode from shared state

title: Login and signup pages
body:
## Description
Build the merchant-facing login and signup pages, wired to the dashboard auth API (see Auth epic). Signup kicks off onboarding; login establishes a dashboard session.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Login form with email/password, inline validation errors
- [ ] Signup form collects business name + email + password, redirects into onboarding flow
- [ ] Handles and displays auth API error responses
- [ ] Basic password strength validation client-side

title: Payments list page with filters
body:
## Description
Paginated list of the merchant's payments with filters for status, payment method, and date range, matching the core API's list endpoint.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Table columns: id, amount, method, status, created_at
- [ ] Filters for status, method, date range persist in the URL query string
- [ ] Pagination (cursor or offset, matching backend)
- [ ] Empty and loading states
- [ ] Clicking a row navigates to the payment detail page

title: Payment detail page with timeline and actions
body:
## Description
Show a single payment's full detail: amount, method-specific details, a timeline of state transitions, and available actions (capture, refund) based on current state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Timeline renders every state transition with timestamp
- [ ] Capture/refund buttons only shown when the payment's state allows them
- [ ] Refund action opens the create-refund flow pre-filled with this payment
- [ ] Shows linked order and any dispute if one exists

title: Orders list page
body:
## Description
List view of Orders with status, amount, and linked payment count, so a merchant can see order-level state separate from individual payment attempts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Table with id, receipt, amount, status, payment attempt count
- [ ] Filter by status and date range
- [ ] Row click navigates to order detail

title: Order detail page
body:
## Description
Show a single order with all payment attempts made against it (useful when a customer retried after a failed card attempt).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Lists every Payment linked to the order with its status
- [ ] Shows order metadata/notes
- [ ] Links out to each payment's detail page

title: Refunds list page
body:
## Description
Dedicated list of refunds (separate from payments) with status, amount, and the originating payment, for merchants reconciling refund activity.

- [ ] Same key + different body returns a conflict error
- [ ] Concurrent replays with the same key don't double-process (race test)
